sentences.text:
appellant-Insurance Company has challenged the judgment/award dated 27.09.2011 passed by [2024:RJ-JD:33727] (2 of 7) [CMA-5384/2011] the learned Judge, MACT, Rajsamand (Raj.) in Claim Case No.28/2010 whereby the learned Tribunal awarded quantum of compensation to the claimants to the tune of Rs.17,04,656/-
along with interest @ 7% p.a. and the liability to pay the compensation was fastened upon the Insurance Company.
2.
Learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company submits that the learned Tribunal has erred while awarding quantum of compensation to the claimants.
He further submits that the learned Tribunal has erred while assessing the income of the deceased, as it is on higher side and is contrary to the Salary Certificate of the deceased (Exhibit-26).

He, thus, urges that the instant misc.
appeal deserves acceptance.
3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants vehemently objects and submits that the learned Tribunal is perfectly justified in awarding quantum of compensation to the claimants.

He further submits that the issue involved in this misc.
appeal is identical to the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Meenakshi Vs.
Oriental Insurance Co.
Ltd. : MANU/SC/0830/2024, wherein, it was observed that "components of house rent allowance,
flexible benefit plan and company contribution to provident fund have to be included in the salary of the deceased while applying the component of rise in income by future prospects to determine the dependency factor".
4.

sentences.text:
The instant misc. appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 ('the Act of 1988') challenging the veracity of the judgment/award dated 26.10.2016 passed by the learned Judge, MACT No.2, Udaipur in MACT Case No.334/2014 whereby claim petition filed by the appellants/claimants herein was partly allowed and the compensation was awarded to the tune of 7,98,600/- @ 7%
per annum and the liability to pay the same was fastened upon the Insurance Company.

2. Brief facts of the case are that on 30.06.2013, while the petitioner Lal Singh along with deceased Heer Singh who happened to be his father-in-law, was going in his The New India Assurance Co. sentences.text: On the way near BSF camp at National Highway, driver of truck bearing registration No.RJ-27- GA-7974 driving in a rash and negligent manner while overtaking the tempo applied sudden breaks and the tempo of Lal Singh collided with the truck from the back side and as a result whereof, Lal Singh sustained grievous injuries and Heer Singh died.

An FIR No.194/2013 was registered at the Police Station Sukher against Sajjan Singh (Driver of the offending vehicle) under Section 279/337, 338 IPC and a charge- sheet was filed after the investigation.

Hence, the appellants claimed for compensation and the held the respondents liable to pay the same jointly and severally.
3. Respondents/Non-claimants Nos.1 and 2 chose not to file reply.

Respondent No.3/Non-claimant- Insurance Company filed the written statement wherein it was admitted that the Insurance Company was the insurer of the offending vehicle but denied the facts regarding age, income, functional disability of injured Lal Singh,
dependency of the claimants on the deceased Heer Singh, etc.

It was further stated that there was a contributory negligence of the driver of the tempo bearing registration No.RJ-27-GA-8663, who was not keeping the safe distance and dashed into the truck from behind as per FIR and also violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance company by the owner was also pleaded by the Insurance Company.
4. As per the pleadings and material available on record, the learned Tribunal framed following issues:-

"(1) Whether on dated 30.06.2013 at about 9.30 PM, driver of Truck of bearing no.RJ-27- GA-7974 while driving the truck in a rash and negligent manner hit the loading tempo thereby caused grievous injuries to Lal Singh and the death of Late Shri Heer Singh.
(2) Whether the R1 was driving the truck under the instructions of R2 the owner of the truck.
(3) Whether the respondents in view of the preliminary objections and reply on merits can be relieved from its liability, if no, its effect.
(4) Whether the petitioners are entitled to get the amount claimed or any other just amount, if yes, then how much amount and from whom.

(5) Relief."
5.
The claimants in support of their claim petition, examined 2 witnesses and exhibited as many as 41 documents to prove their case.
No evidence on behalf of respondents Nos.1 and 2 and the insurance company was produced.

6. After hearing both the parties, the learned Tribunal awarded claimants compensation to the tune of 7,98,600/- @ 7% per annum and the liability to pay the same was fastened upon the Insurance Company and thus, being dissatisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the learned The New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs Smt. Pushplata And Ors. ... on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/193827262/
3 Tribunal, the claimants have preferred the instant misc. appeal.

sentences.text: 7. Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants submits that the quantum of compensation as awarded by the learned Tribunal is not as per the material available on record.

In furtherance thereof, he submits that the learned Tribunal has committed a grave error in assessing the income of the deceased because the deceased was earning more at the time of untoward incident and there was every likelihood of advancement in his career as he was a hard working person aged 47 years.
He also submits that the learned Tribunal also not considered the future prospects.

8. In support of his arguments, counsel for the appellants has placed reliance upon the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Rajwati @ Rajjo & Ors. Vs. United India Insurance Company Ltd. & Ors. : 2023 (1) RAR 20 wherein it was held that :-
"xxxx.
19.

entities.text: Rajwati @ Rajjo & Ors. Vs. United India Insurance Company Ltd. & Ors. : 2023 (1) RAR 20
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is well settled that Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is a beneficial piece of legislation and as such, while dealing with compensation cases, once the actual occurrence of the accident has been established, the Tribunal's role would be to [2024:RJ-JD:33727] (5 of 7) [CMA-5384/2011] award just and fair compensation.

As held by this Court in Sunita (supra) and Kusum Lata (supra), strict rules of evidence as applicable in a criminal trial, are not applicable in motor accident compensation cases, i.e. to say,
"the standard of proof to be borne in mind must be of preponderance of probability and not the strict standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt which is followed in criminal cases".
20.

In view of the above, we do not agree with the view taken by the High Court while rejecting the salary certificate (Exhibit 19) and pay slip (Exhibit 20) of the deceased merely on the ground that the person issuing the two aforementioned documents was not examined before the Learned Tribunal.
The said documents are conclusive proof of the income of the deceased and were also corroborated by the statements of the deceased's wife (Appellant No.1 herein) and his co-workers.
As such, the High Court was not justified in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.4,836/- per month on the basis of minimum wages fixed by the State at the relevant time.
Resultantly, we affirm the findings of the Learned Tribunal so far as they relate to assessing the deceased's income at Rs.11,225/- per month on the basis of aforementioned two documents.

Annual income of the deceased, therefore, amounts to, Rs.11,225/- x 12 = Rs.1,34,700/-.
xxxx."
9.

He also places reliance upon the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court on 23.07.2024 in the case of Meenakshi Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. :
MANU/SC/0830/2024, wherein, it was observed that "components of house rent allowance, flexible benefit plan and company contribution to provident fund have to be included in the salary of the deceased while applying the component of rise in The New India Assurance Co. Ltd vs Smt. Pushplata And Ors.

10. Learned counsel for the appellants, thus, craves indulgence of this Court to quash and set aside the impugned judgment/award dated 26.10.2016 passed by the learned Judge, MACT No.2, Udaipur in MACT Case No.334/2014 and allow the instant misc. appeal.
11. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent- Insurance Company opposes the submissions advanced by the appellants' counsel and submits that the instant misc. appeal warrants rejection.

I have given my thoughtful consideration to the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the material available on record as well as the judgments cited at Bar.
13.

It is apparent that the deceased at the time of the incident, was 47 years of age and was earning 9,975/- (total salary) which is more than what was assessed by the learned Tribunal and he also had every likelihood of advancement in his career and thus, while disbelieving the documentary evidence produced by the claimants i.e. Exhibits-40 & 41 (salary certificate and salary slip respectively), the learned Tribunal has wrongfully assessed income of the deceased while keeping in view the prevalent minimum wages at the time of the accident, which is not agreed upon by this Court, as the law is well settled in the case of Rajwati @ Rajjo (supra).
Hence, this Court finds considerable force in the arguments advanced by the claimants/appellants with regard to assessment of income of the deceased.

14. Since there is no dispute on the factual matrix of the case, both the counsel were directed to submit the calculation of the compensation awardable to the claimants, afresh in light of the guidelines laid down by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. : (2017)16 SCC 680, Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation :
AIR 2009 SC 3104, coupled with the judgments passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of Rajwati @ Rajjo (supra) and Meenakshi (supra), the said calculation has been furnished in a tabular form, which is as follows:-
Monthly salary of the deceased inclusive 9,975/- house rent allowance, flexible benefit plan and contribution to provident fund (Add) 30% of rise in income towards 12,968/- future prospects i.e. 2,993/-
 (Less) deduction of 1/3rd i.e. 4,322/- 8,646/-(net  income after  deduction)
Multiplied by 12 (annual salary) and 13 13,48,776/- (as per age at the time of accident) (Less) Already awarded by the Tribunal 7,98,600/-
Enhanced Amount (round figure) 5,50,176/-

sentences.text: Accordingly, the instant misc. appeal is partly allowed in the above terms and the judgment/award dated 26.10.2016 passed by the learned Judge, MACT No.2, Udaipur in MACT Case No.334/2014, is partially modified accordingly.
The enhanced amount of Rs.5,50,176/- shall carry interest @ 6% per annum [2024:RJ-JD:33727] (7 of 7) [CMA-5384/2011] from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of deposit.

The enhanced amount shall be deposited by the respondent-Insurance Company with the learned Tribunal within a period of six weeks from today failing which, the interest shall stand enhanced @ 7.5% per annum from the date of this order till actual realization.
16.
The Insurance Company shall pay the enhanced compensation to the appellants-claimants and therefore, shall recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
17. Any amount already paid by the respondent- Insurance Company, shall be adjusted towards the amount finally awarded by this Court.
18. No order as to costs.

19. Record be returned to the Tribunal forthwith."
6.

Thus, in view of the aforequoted judgment i.e. Smt. Kamla Bai (supra) coupled with the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Meenakshi (supra), the instant misc.
appeal is also dismissed in the same terms.

7. The impugned award dated 27.09.2011 passed by the learned MACT, Rajsamand (Raj.) in Claim Case No.28/2010 does not suffers from any illegality or any infirmity whatsoever warranting interference therein.
8. Stay application as well as all other pending application(s), if any, also stand dismissed.
9. No order as to costs.
